# Agent instructions

<!-- aspire:begin (generated by the Aspire CLI; `aspire new` and `aspire agent init` replace the text up to aspire:end) -->
## Aspire

This is an Aspire application. Its AppHost is `StarterApp.AppHost/StarterApp.AppHost.csproj`.

### Run it
1. Start it: `aspire start --apphost StarterApp.AppHost/StarterApp.AppHost.csproj --non-interactive --isolated`.
2. `aspire describe --apphost StarterApp.AppHost/StarterApp.AppHost.csproj` lists every resource of the running app
   with its state, health and endpoint URLs. That list names the resources to wait on.
3. `aspire wait <resource-name> --apphost StarterApp.AppHost/StarterApp.AppHost.csproj` for each resource the task needs,
   with `<resource-name>` taken from that list. It returns when the resource is healthy.

`aspire logs <resource-name> --apphost StarterApp.AppHost/StarterApp.AppHost.csproj` prints that resource's console output.

### When it is slow
Start with `aspire otel traces -n 15 --search "duration:>500" --apphost StarterApp.AppHost/StarterApp.AppHost.csproj`
(milliseconds; lower the threshold if nothing comes back), before reading code or timing requests by hand.

Aspire skills are provided by the `microsoft/aspire-skills` plugin that `aspire agent init` registered, and the harness lists them.
